findings.title: Task 13/14 rely on a `/timed out/i` pattern that does not exist
findings.description:
Task 13 says the timeout message gets remediation text because "the `/timed out/i` pattern already matches". `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS` actually contains `/connection timed out/i` and `/etimedout/i`. A message like "git … timed out after 60 seconds" matches neither, so `withNetworkErrorHint` returns it unchanged.

Task 14 then asserts the message contains `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION`, which will fail. The design (D10) carries the same error.

Fix: Task 13 needs an explicit step to add a timeout pattern to `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS`, or to word the message so an existing pattern matches.

findings.title: Task 15/17 leave the D10 timeout unwired and untested
findings.description:
Task 15 contradicts itself. It gives the signature `init(operationPath: string)` and says it runs with `{ timeoutMs: GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS }`, then says the timeout is passed "as an `init()` option" so `sync()` stays unbounded. The signature has no options parameter and the default is not stated.

Task 17 calls `SubmoduleStrategy.init(operationPath)` with no option. If the default is unbounded, auto-init inside `cf build` and the MCP tools is unbounded and D10 is unmet.

No test catches this: Tasks 16 and 18 never assert that the auto-init path passes a timeout or that `sync()` does not.

Fix: state the signature and default in Task 15, have Task 17 pass the timeout explicitly, and add one assertion for each path.

findings.title: Task 11 makes `detect()` throw, widening failure beyond the design
findings.description:
The design's data flow puts the `'error'` → throw inside `ensureCheckout()`. Task 11 moves it into `detect()`, which is also called by `cf guides info`, `guide_status`, `setup-ide`, install and update. Any `git submodule status` failure would now fail those status commands, where every other git call in `detect()` degrades to `null`.

It also breaks existing tests. The task file notes that `GuideDetector.test.ts` mocks the filesystem; a mocked submodule case would now run real `git submodule status` against a non-repo, get `'error'`, and throw. No step in Task 11 or 12 updates the mocked suites in core, CLI or MCP, and Task 11's success criterion runs no tests.

Fix: either keep `detect()` non-throwing and throw in `ensureCheckout()` as designed, or add a step to mock `checkSyncStatus` in the existing suites.

findings.title: Task 26 (and Task 7) break the omitted-flag path
findings.description:
Task 26 says to pass `normalizeGuideMethod(opts.strategy)` into `guidesInstallAction`. `--strategy` is optional and `init.ts:118` currently calls `guidesInstallAction(cwd)` with no options. Followed literally, plain `cf init` would call `normalizeGuideMethod(undefined)`, which Tasks 1 and 2 define as throwing.

Task 7 has the same wording for `guides.ts:125`. Neither Task 8 nor Task 27 includes a no-flag case.

Fix: say "normalize only when provided; undefined falls through to config", and add a no-flag test.

The alias check and stderr warning are also specified separately in `guides.ts` (Task 7) and `init.ts` (Task 26). Put them once in `guidesInstallAction`, taking the raw string, so they are not duplicated.

findings.title: Task 5 does not cover the no-`configManager` branch
findings.description:
`resolveStrategy()` returns the `'submodule'` literal at line 196 both when the config read fails and when `this.configManager` is undefined. Task 5 says to delete the literal because "no fallback branch is needed", which only holds when a config manager exists. `resolveSource()` has the same shape at lines 170-182.

Fix: state what happens without a config manager (read `ConfigKeys['guide.git_strategy'].default` directly, or make the manager required), and add that case to Task 6.

Task 5 also leaves the return shape open ("choose one … e.g."). Tasks 6 and 7 depend on it, so pin it in the task.

findings.title: Task 7 adds a third `'manual'` literal that fails Task 32's own grep
findings.description:
The technical criterion is "no `'manual'` literal outside the alias table and enum". Task 7 hard-codes `['submodule', 'clone', 'tarball', 'manual']` in the MCP zod enum, duplicating the `ConfigKeys` list. Task 32 then asks to confirm the criterion, which that literal fails.

Fix: build the zod enum from the canonical method list plus the keys of `GUIDE_METHOD_DEPRECATED_ALIASES`, and state the grep's expected hits consistently across Tasks 3, 7 and 32.

findings.title: Commit markers are embedded in checkbox sub-items
findings.description:
All commit points are written as "Success criteria: … Commit: `…`" inside checkbox lines (Tasks 4, 6, 8, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 23, 24, 27, 29, 31), so checking the box conflates verification with committing. Placement is good: each sits after a test task at a working point.

Fix: move each to a plain `**Commit**:` line after the task.

Task 32's success criterion also includes "PM reviews before merge to `main`". That is a process gate, not a verifiable criterion; drop it.

findings.title: Several tasks are too granular or not independently completable
findings.description:
- **Task 10 into 11:** Task 10's success criterion is "typecheck passes once Task 11 populates the field", so it cannot be completed alone.
- **Task 1 into 3:** Task 1 deliberately leaves core failing typecheck until Task 3.
- **Tasks 28+29 and 30+31:** each is an effort-1 pair that can be one task.

That brings 32 tasks to about 27 with no loss of coverage. The rest of the count is proportionate to a three-issue slice spanning core, CLI and MCP.

findings.title: Config-path alias warning has no CLI or MCP test
findings.description: The criterion "shared config has `guide.git_strategy: manual` → installs as tarball with the same warning" is tested only in core (Task 6b, alias reported). Task 8 covers the flag path only. One CLI case asserting the stderr warning for the config path would close it. Task 7 also does not say whether MCP `guide_install` adds a notice for the config-sourced alias, which D5 implies.

findings.title: Task 20's enumerated call sites omit `phaseShorthand.ts`
findings.description: The grep Task 20 mandates will hit this file, which reads `PROMPT_FILE_RELATIVE_PATH`, and the "cover every hit" rule handles it. The explicit list (`build.ts`, `prompt.ts`, `setup-ide.ts`) does not name it, so add it to avoid a literal reading skipping it.

findings.title: Success-criteria coverage and sequencing
findings.description:
- **Coverage:** all ten functional criteria map to tasks: auto-init to 17–21, `--json` to 21, read-only info to 24, out-of-sync to 17/18/21, alias to 5–8, `init --strategy` to 26/27, help to 25/27, managed notice to 28–30, malformed config to 5/6. The Task 6(c) mock is a fair stand-in because `ConfigManager.ts:24-29` rethrows parse errors.
- **Technical criteria:** the test list and docs are covered, with Task 32 as the walkthrough.
- **Sequencing:** order matches the design's Implementation Notes, test tasks follow their implementation tasks, and there are no circular dependencies or scope creep.
- **MCP call sites:** the two lines Task 22 names (`contextTools.ts:57` and `:98`) are the only hits in `mcp-server/src`.
